prompt: Draw a geometric diagram showing two circles labeled X and Y, with an external point T. From T, draw two tangents to each circle: to circle X, the tangents touch at points C and S; to circle Y, the tangents touch at points A and E. Clearly label all points (X, Y, T, C, S, A, E). The tangents from T to each circle should not intersect except at T, and the circles should not overlap. The configuration should make it clear that TA and TC are tangents to circle Y and X respectively, and TS and TE are tangents to circle X and Y respectively.

Draw a geometric diagram of a right circular cone with a height of 16 units and a base radius of 4 units. Shade a horizontal cross-section at height h from the vertex, and clearly indicate the height (16), the base radius (4), and the variable height h. Use dashed lines to show the radius and height from the vertex to the base and to the cross-section.

Draw a three-dimensional geometric diagram of a non-right hexagonal prism, where the base is a regular hexagon labeled ABCDEF lying flat on the ground. The vertical edges at vertices A, B, and C have heights of 12, 9, and 10 units, respectively, and the top face is a hexagon that is not parallel to the base. Clearly indicate the correspondence between the top and bottom vertices, and label the heights at A, B, and C.

Draw a three-dimensional diagram of a prism whose base is an isosceles trapezoid with a bottom base of 3 units, top base of 3 + 2h units, and non-parallel sides each of length h, where the base angles adjacent to the bottom base are 45°. The height of the prism is 20 units. Also, provide a two-dimensional cross-sectional view of the base, clearly labeling all relevant dimensions and angles.

Draw a three-dimensional geometric diagram showing two planes, R and S, intersecting along line segment DE, and A is on DE. In plane R, draw line segment FJ passing through point A and perpendicular to plane S. In plane S, draw line segments BC and DE, both passing through point A. Label all points (A, B, C, D, E, F, J) and planes (R, S) clearly. Use dashed lines to indicate hidden edges.

Draw a three-dimensional geometric diagram showing three distinct planes labeled \\(\\mathscr{P}\\), Q, and R, such that a straight line \\(\\overleftrightarrow{EF}\\) passes through all three planes. The line \\(\\overleftrightarrow{EF}\\) should be perpendicular to both planes \\(\\mathscr{P}\\) and R, with E at the left of P and F at the right of R. P also intersect plane Q between E and F. Clearly indicate the intersection points and label all planes and points as specified.

Draw the region in the polar coordinate plane that lies inside the curve given by \( r = 1 - \sin\\theta \) and outside the circle \( r = 1 \). Clearly indicate the shaded region that represents the area between these two curves.

Draw a rectangle with side lengths 8 units (horizontal) and 5 units (vertical). On the top and bottom sides, mark segments of 1 unit from the left and right corners. On the left and right sides, mark segments of 1 unit from the top and bottom corners. Connect the 1-unit mark on the top side to the 1-unit mark on the right side, and connect the 1-unit mark on the left side to the 1-unit mark on the bottom side. Shade the regions that are bounded by the rectangle and these two lines but do not overlap with the central region.

Draw a diagram of a baseball diamond represented as a square with each side measuring 90 feet. Label the four vertices as Home plate (H), First base (I), Second base (II), and Third base (III). Draw and label the following: (1) a dashed line from H to II, (2) a line from H to a point R on the segment from II to III, (3) label the distance from II to R as x, the distance from H to R as u.

Draw an isosceles trapezoid ABCD with BC parallel to AD and AB = CD. On diagonal AC, mark points X and Y such that X is between A and Y, angle AXD = angle BYC = 90°, AX = 3, XY = 1, and YC = 2. Clearly indicate all right angles and label all given segment lengths.

Given a square ABCD with side length 4√5, let E be the midpoint of side CD. Draw diagonal AC and line BE, intersecting at point M. On side AD, mark a point F. Draw line BF, which intersects AC at G and AE at H. Construct BF such that BF is perpendicular to AE at H. Connect MH. From M, draw a perpendicular to AE, meeting AE at N. Clearly label all points A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, M, and N, and indicate all right angles.

Construct a geometric figure as follows: Draw a circle with diameter AB = 8, and let O be its center. Draw a tangent AE at point A, with AE = 2√7. Construct rhombus ACDE with AE as one side and C lying on the circle. Let CD intersect AB at F. Connect CE and extend it to meet the circle again at G. Connect GF. Draw OC, BG, and AG. Draw CI perpendicular to EA, meeting the extension of EA at I. Draw GH perpendicular to EA at H, and extend GH to meet the extension of CD at J. Label all points.

In a square ABCD, let points E and F be on sides BC and AB, respectively. Draw segments DE, CF, and EF such that DE is perpendicular to CF. Let G and H be the midpoints of CF and DE, respectively. Connect GH. From H, draw HQ perpendicular to BC at Q; from G, draw GT perpendicular to BC at T; and from G, draw GK perpendicular to CD at K. Clearly label all points and indicate right angles where appropriate.

Given a circle with center O and radius 2√3, draw its diameter AB. Let C be the midpoint of OB. Through C, draw a line perpendicular to OB, intersecting the circle at points D and E. Let F be a point on the circle. Connect FD. Through A, draw a line perpendicular to AB, extending to meet the extension of FD at point H, such that DH = 3√7. From D, draw DG perpendicular to AH at G. From F, draw FQ perpendicular to DE, meeting DE at M. From O, draw OQ perpendicular to FQ, with the two lines intersecting at Q. Label all points.

Given a square ABCD with side length 4, let E be the midpoint of side AB. Draw line CE. From point B, draw a perpendicular BF to CE, meeting at F. Connect DF. From point A, draw a perpendicular AH to DF, meeting at H. Extend AH to intersect CE at M and BC at N. Extend DF to intersect AB at P. Label all points (A, B, C, D, E, F, H, M, N, P) clearly. Indicate all right angles with appropriate marks.

Draw a circle labeled O with points A, B, C, and D on its circumference such that chords AB and CD intersect at point E inside the circle. From an external point F, draw a secant passing through points D, A, and extending to F, and a tangent from F touching the circle at B. Also, draw chord AC. Label all points (A, B, C, D, E, F, O).
